div.div:
1 نَكِدَ , aor.
نَكَدَ , (S, K, &c.,) inf. n. نَكَدٌ, (S, L, Msb,) It (a man's life) was, or became, hard, or strait, and difficult. (S, L, Msb, K.) ―
-b2- نَكِدَ It (a she-camel's milk) became deficient. (R.) ―
-b3- نَكِدَ It (water) became exhausted. (A.) ―
-b4- نَكِدَتِ الرَّكِيَّةُ The well came to have little water. (S, L, K.) ―
-b5- نَكِدَ, aor.
نَكَدَ , inf. n. نَكَدٌ, He was, or became, unpropitious, and mean: (L:) he became hard, or difficult: (Msb:) he gave little: or gave not at all: you say also نَكِدَ بِحَاجَتِنَا he was niggardly of that which we wanted. (L.) ―
-b6- نَكَدَ حَاجَتَهُ, aor.
نَكُدَ ; (K;) or نَكَدَهُ حَاجَتَهُ, (L,) He withheld from him, or refused him, his want. (L, K.) ―
-b7- نَكَدَهُ, aor.
نَكُدَ , He withheld from him, or refused him, what he asked: or [in the CK, and] the same, (K,) or نَكَدَهُ مَا سَأَلَهُ, aor.
نَكُدَ , inf. n. نَكْدٌ, (L,) he gave him not save the least of what he asked. (L, K.) ―
-b8- نُكِدَ, [in measure] like عُنِىَ, He had many askers and gave little. (K.) ―
-b9- نَكَدَ, aor.
نَكُدَ , He (a raven or crow) croaked with his utmost force; (A, K;) as though vomiting; as also ↓ تنكّد . (A.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
